title: TestSuite
description:
The TestSuite class represents a single suite. This class is only available in the main thread. Refer to the "Runner API" if you are working with runtime tasks.

entries.name: TestSuite
entries.description:
The TestSuite class represents a single suite. This class is only available in the main thread. Refer to the "Runner API" if you are working with runtime tasks.

The TestSuite instance always has a type property with the value of suite. You can use it to distinguish between different task types:

children.name: project
children.description: This references the TestProject that the test belongs to.

children.name: module
children.description: This is a direct reference to the TestModule where the test is defined.

children.name: name
children.description: This is a suite name that was passed to the describe function.

children.name: fullName
children.description: The name of the suite including all parent suites separated with > symbol. This suite has a full name "the validation logic > validating cities":

children.name: id
children.description:
This is suite's unique identifier. This ID is deterministic and will be the same for the same suite across multiple runs. The ID is based on the project name, module ID and suite order.

The ID looks like this:

examples.code:
1223128da3_0_0_0
^^^^^^^^^^ the file hash
           ^ suite index
             ^ nested suite index
               ^ test index

notes: DANGERDon't try to parse the ID. It can have a minus at the start: -1223128da3_0_0_0.

children.name: location
children.description:
The location in the module where the suite was defined. Locations are collected only if includeTaskLocation is enabled in the config. Note that this option is automatically enabled if --reporter=html, --ui or --browser flags are used.

The location of this suite will be equal to { line: 3, column: 1 }:

children.name: parent
children.description: Parent suite. If the suite was called directly inside the module, the parent will be the module itself.

children.name: options
children.description: The options that suite was collected with.
signatures:
interface TaskOptions {
  readonly each: boolean | undefined
  readonly fails: boolean | undefined
  readonly concurrent: boolean | undefined
  readonly shuffle: boolean | undefined
  readonly retry: number | undefined
  readonly repeats: number | undefined
  readonly tags: string[] | undefined
  readonly mode: 'run' | 'only' | 'skip' | 'todo'
}

children.name: children
children.description: This is a collection of all suites and tests inside the current suite.

children.name: ok
children.description: Checks if the suite has any failed tests. This will also return false if suite failed during collection. In that case, check the errors() for thrown errors.

children.name: state
children.description: Checks the running state of the suite. Possible return values:
notes: pending: the tests in this suite did not finish running yet.
failed: this suite has failed tests or they couldn't be collected. If errors() is not empty, it means the suite failed to collect tests.
passed: every test inside this suite has passed.
skipped: this suite was skipped during collection.
WARNINGNote that test module also has a state method that returns the same values, but it can also return an additional queued state if the module wasn't executed yet.

children.name: errors
children.description: Errors that happened outside of the test run during collection, like syntax errors.
notes: WARNINGNote that errors are serialized into simple objects: instanceof Error will always return false.

children.name: meta 3.1.0+
children.description:
Custom metadata that was attached to the suite during its execution or collection. Since Vitest 4.1, the meta can be attached by providing a meta object during test collection:

Note that suite metadata will be inherited by tests since Vitest 4.1.
notes: TIPIf metadata was attached during collection (outside of the test function), then it will be available in onTestModuleCollected hook in the custom reporter.
